contracts.commit_point: target.read_text(encoding='utf-8') in read_file (native.py:97) and target.parent.mkdir(...)/target.write_text(...) in write_file (native.py:121-122), each reached only after resolve_under succeeds. Both commit points share the same stratum, so one contract covers them.
contracts.declared_mechanism: resolve_under(root, user_path) (native.py:16-24) resolves the candidate against the resolved root and raises ValueError unless the candidate equals the root or has the root among its resolved parents; each tool calls resolve_under on the agent-supplied path before its effect (read_file at native.py:90, write_file at native.py:120, _list_files_result at native.py:36) and converts exceptions into tool_error payloads.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A filesystem effect (directory listing, read_text, mkdir/write_text) on a candidate path whose resolved form is neither equal to the resolved project root nor contained within it — resolve_under raises ValueError('Path is outside configured project-root').

contracts.protected_operation: Directory enumeration and file read/write performed by the @agent.tool functions list_files, read_file, and write_file with agent-supplied path (and content) arguments.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent file tools (list_files, read_file, write_file) must only enumerate, read, or write paths that resolve to cfg.project_root or inside it; any resolved path outside the project root must raise before the filesystem effect occurs. (Preserved from the phase-two reviewer rationale: 'resolve_under similarly confines file tools to project_root'; the reviewer did not state it as a standalone obligation.)
scope_limits: Containment-only guard: once the resolved path is inside the root, no constraints on file size, content, or overwriting existing files; write_file creates parent directories after the guard passes.
Registration of these file tools into the studied runtime depends on register_runtime_tools wiring that is not shown in the supplied views.
The list_files effect (rglob/iterdir enumeration) is read-only; only write_file mutates the filesystem.

contracts.commit_point: The run_shell_fn(command=..., cwd=cfg.project_root, timeout_sec=..., shell_mode=..., shell_override=...) call inside _run_allowed_shell (lllars_core/tools/shell_runtime_policy.py:121-127); the canonicalize/match/reject decision at lines 114-120 strictly precedes and gates it.
contracts.declared_mechanism: make_allowed_shell_runner (lllars_core/tools/shell_runtime_policy.py:108-132) constructs _run_allowed_shell, which canonicalizes the requested command via the injected canonicalize_shell_command, matches it against cfg.allowed_shell_commands via _match_allowlist_pattern, and, when no pattern matches, returns .dumps(_rejected_allowlist_payload()) — returncode 126, empty stdout, '[lllars] rejected shell command: not in allowlist.' stderr — without calling run_shell_fn; build_agent constructs the runner with the canonicalizer and run_shell injection (agent_builder.py:158-165) and wires it into tool registration as run_allowed_shell (agent_builder.py:199-208).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Invocation of run_shell for a command whose canonicalized form neither equals an allowlist pattern nor starts with the text preceding the first '*' wildcard in any pattern of cfg.allowed_shell_commands, i.e. _match_allowlist_pattern returning None.

Whether cfg.test_command and cfg.eval_command are members of cfg.allowed_shell_commands; if not, run_test_command / run_eval_command would be rejected on every call.

contracts.protected_operation: Shell command execution requested by the model via the registered agent tools run_allowlisted_shell (agent-supplied command text or allowlist command_id) and run_test_command / run_eval_command (cfg.test_command / cfg.eval_command).
contracts.protected_resource: The OS shell execution channel reached through run_shell (lllars_core.shell), invoked with cwd=cfg.project_root and the configured shell_mode / shell_override.
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-initiated shell execution through the allowlisted runner tools (run_allowlisted_shell, run_test_command, run_eval_command) must not reach the run_shell effect unless the canonicalized command matches an entry in cfg.allowed_shell_commands; unmatched commands must be denied with a returncode-126 rejection payload before any process is spawned. (Merges the phase-one and phase-two reviewer wordings, which describe the same guard and commit point.)
scope_limits: The guard protects only the allowed runner: make_unrestricted_shell_runner (shell_runtime_policy.py:135-149) performs no allowlist check, build_agent constructs and passes run_unrestricted_shell unconditionally (agent_builder.py:199-208), and register_shell_tools registers run_unrestricted_shell whenever a runner is supplied (shell_policy.py:190-196).
Matching semantics are exact equality or wildcard-prefix (text before the first '*'); a '*' pattern authorizes every command sharing that prefix (shell_runtime_policy.py:82-94).

Rejection is a returned JSON payload to the model (returncode 126), not an exception or harness-level block; registration is gated only on cfg.allowed_shell_commands being non-empty and cfg.test_command / cfg.eval_command being non-null (shell_policy.py:185-203).
No claim is made about post-execution behavior, output sanitization, or timeout enforcement inside run_shell itself.
